Portfolio Genesis
July – September 2019
The Journey Begins
Armstrong Capital onboarded the Prasad family. Divya's portfolio was transferred from HSBC and strategically restructured — funds were parked in liquid funds first, then systematically transferred into equity via STP (Systematic Transfer Plan), a method that reduces timing risk. Usha's portfolio was structured with a moderate risk approach — a blend of debt and hybrid funds with a measured equity allocation.

Damodaran Joins the Portfolio
Mr. Damodaran Babu Krishnaprasad joined as the third portfolio member. His portfolio was designed with a conservative-moderate approach — primarily debt instruments (Low Duration, Ultra Short Duration) supplemented with Arbitrage funds. This diversification added stability to the family's overall wealth structure.

Portfolio at All-Time High

Capital Protection Move
March 16, 2020
Strategic Portfolio Protection — COVID-19
As global markets entered unprecedented volatility amid the COVID-19 pandemic (Sensex fell ~28% from peak), Armstrong Capital took a decisive protective action. The entire equity and hybrid portfolio was moved to debt instruments — specifically liquid and ultra short duration funds. This preserved the family's capital during one of the most turbulent market periods in history. The Sensex had crashed to ~29,468 from its January high of ~41,000.

Recovery Phase
Dec 2020 – Dec 2021
Gradual Re-Entry & Near Breakeven
With markets recovering, January 2021 saw a measured restructuring — carefully re-introducing hybrid and balanced advantage funds. By December 2021, the portfolio had navigated back to near-breakeven with a small positive alpha. This period also marked the introduction of international equity exposure (PGIM Global Equity for Usha, Nippon India US Equity for Divya). Sensex by Dec 2021 had surged to 58,283 — well above pre-COVID levels.

Restructuring I
June 2022
First Equity Re-Entry — STP Strategy
Armstrong Capital executed the first meaningful equity reintroduction via a 50/50 approach: 50% immediate lump-sum switches into equity funds, and 50% via systematic STP over 50 weeks. New equity funds were introduced across market capitalizations — Large Cap, Large & Mid Cap, Mid Cap — along with an international NASDAQ 100 fund for Divya. Family portfolio: ₹3.07 Cr.

Portfolio Back on Growth Track
The equity re-entry from June 2022 was bearing fruit. The family portfolio stood at ₹3.21 Crore with an absolute return of 8.83% and XIRR of 4.51%. Damodaran's portfolio led with an XIRR of 5.66%, while equity positions across all members were steadily appreciating. The portfolio's equity weight had grown to 29–37% across members.

Major Restructuring II
July 2023
Bold Pivot — Wealth Creation Mode
The most comprehensive restructuring of the journey. Debt allocation was dramatically reduced from ~60% to just 20%, with domestic equity raised to 47–60% across members. A 70-week STP engine was deployed, systematically moving funds from debt to a diversified equity basket spanning Large Cap, Mid Cap, Small Cap, Flexi Cap, Contra, Multi Cap, and Large & Mid Cap. Family value at this point: ₹3.39 Cr.

Restructuring III — Complete
January 2024
Debt Eliminated — Full Growth Mode
The final and most decisive restructuring. All remaining debt was exited across all three portfolios. The deployment was swift — 25-week STPs at accelerated weekly amounts (Usha ₹91,500/week, Damodaran ₹53,600/week). New equity funds were added — Baroda BNP Large Cap, ITI Mid Cap (Usha), Bandhan Core Equity, Motilal Multi Cap (Damodaran). The family portfolio crossed ₹4 Crore for the first time.

Market Resilience
Navigating the COVID-19 Storm
Strategic Capital Protection
When Markets Fell, the Portfolio Stood Firm
March 2020 brought one of the most severe market corrections in history. The Sensex fell nearly 28% from its January 2020 high. At this critical juncture, Armstrong Capital proactively moved the entire Prasad family portfolio to the safety of debt instruments — preserving capital during the most uncertain phase.
This decisive action ensured the portfolio navigated the storm with dignity. As markets recovered through 2020–2021, the portfolio was gradually reintroduced to hybrid and equity — capturing the recovery rally while maintaining a foundation of stability.

💡 A Reflective Perspective — The Benefit of Hindsight
Markets, as we now know, recovered faster than most anticipated. The Sensex crossed 45,000 by December 2020 — well above its pre-COVID levels. In hindsight, staying invested through the volatility would have captured this recovery directly.
Every market cycle teaches us something valuable. The March 2020 decision to protect capital was made at a moment of genuine global uncertainty — when the duration and depth of the economic impact was truly unknown. What this period ultimately demonstrated is that once stability returned, a well-structured, equity-focused portfolio could rebuild and then significantly outperform — which is precisely what the Prasad family portfolio has achieved in the years since. The journey from ₹2.89 Cr in March 2020 to ₹5.05 Cr in May 2026 — a growth of 74.7% in six years — is a testament to that resilience and the power of disciplined long-term investing.

💡
A Gentle Reflection — The Market Taught Us Something Valuable
The decision to protect in March 2020 was made under extraordinary global uncertainty — when no one could predict the depth or duration of the pandemic's economic impact. Markets, as history has shown, recovered with remarkable speed. If the portfolio had simply stayed invested through that turbulent period, the natural recovery would have done the work. The key insight this journey offers: time in the market, rather than timing the market, tends to be the greatest wealth creator. The portfolio's strong performance from 2023 to 2026 — driven by a fully equity-oriented strategy — is itself the proof. The Prasad family is now firmly on the right path, and the years ahead look encouraging.
